messages:
Marta: quick triage — need to pick the quant plan for nova-13B intake. primary goals: stay within dedicated cost targets for Q2, avoid >1.5% end-to-end quality regressions on our chat eval, and support 8k+ contexts for enterprise customers.
Raj: timeline? who needs this in prod first?
Marta: short answer: Platform team wants a fastpath baseline for early adopters by EOD Friday. If we can show a safe fallback + perf numbers, sales can demo. Long answer: we also need a longer sweep next week for hybrid configs.
Simon: propose two lanes:
  - fastpath (low ops): GGUF int8 symmetric probe + baseline fp16 for regression checks
  - slowpath (quality-aware): fp8 hybrid (quantized weights, fp32 accum) with length-aware calibration
Elaine: agree. fastpath gives us cost wins quickly; slowpath for customers that care about quality.
Marta: ok. what exact experiments for fastpath? we should minimize the run time (compute) but get representative diffs.
Simon: fastpath experiments:
  1) fp16 baseline (short-run, 500 prompts)
  2) int8-gguf (post-training quant, static calib with 2% of samples)
  3) int8-gguf + KV cache disabled (to simulate streaming edge case)
metrics: token-latency, p50/p95, chrF/ROUGE diff vs baseline, and our chat-quality regression harness (threshold 1.5%).
Elaine: include a small prompt set of 120 length-stratified queries (short/med/long) + 30 instruction-following hardcases.
Raj: who runs the calibration and where do we store artifacts?
Marta: Raj — can you kick off the fastpath pipeline? put artifacts in s3://redwood-ml/quant-probes/nova13b/fastpath/<run_ts>/ . Add a manifest with the model hashes and gguf file names.
Raj: ack. I'll run on a single A100 pool first. command I'm going to use:
```
python tools/quant_probe.py --model checkpoints/nova13b/checkpoint.bin \
  --calib-samples 200 --gguf-out out/nova13b-int8.gguf \
  --evalset data/qa-length-stratified-120.jsonl --outdir s3://redwood-ml/quant-probes/nova13b/fastpath/$TS
```
Marta: for fastpath, reduce calib-samples to 50 to speed it up, but include the 30 hardcases Elaine mentioned. we care about signal not perfect calibration.
Raj: got it. changing to --calib-samples 50.
Simon: for slowpath (next week) we'll run an FP8 hybrid sweep with per-layer scaling and per-head sensitivity. schedule it as a batch: 3 seeds x 4 quant profiles.
Elaine: add a check in the harness to compute hallucination rate on the hardcases. last time fp8 had a subtle hallucination bump on a few math prompts.
Marta: good call. add alerting: if hallucination_rate_delta > 0.6% or rouge_drop > 1.5% then mark as regression and block rollout.
calib-bot: run-complete summary for run 2853179000
  run_id: probe-2853179000
  artifacts: s3://redwood-ml/quant-probes/nova13b/fastpath/2853179000/
  metrics:
    baseline_fp16: p50=42ms p95=110ms, chat_regression=0.0%
    int8_gguf: p50=28ms p95=78ms, chat_regression=0.9%, rouge_drop=0.8%, hallucination_delta=0.1%
    int8_gguf_kv_off: p50=27ms p95=85ms, chat_regression=1.2%, rouge_drop=1.1%, hallucination_delta=0.3%
  note: int8_gguf passes fastpath thresholds but kv_off variant is close to the 1.5% ceiling.
Marta: nice. initial signal looks acceptable for fastpath. plan: ship int8-gguf as experimental variant with rollout=10% and runtime fallback to fp16 if chat_regression > 1.5% on live eval.
Simon: agree but add a per-route length-aware policy: for requests >6k tokens force fp16/fp8-hybrid (cost spike but keep quality). For <=6k use int8-gguf.
Elaine: I'll add the length-aware policy to the routing config. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/platform/pull/4226 — will add tests.
Raj: starting the slowpath fp8 sweep in the afternoon. I'll use the harness job:
```
jobs/submit --job quant-sweep --model nova13b --profiles fp8-hybrid-001,fp8-hybrid-002 --seeds 3 --out s3://redwood-ml/quant-probes/nova13b/slowpath/$TS
```
Marta: assign ownership:
  - Raj: run fastpath + slowpath jobs and upload artifacts
  - Simon: add the slowpath eval configs & sensitivity script to the repo
  - Elaine: routing policy + alert thresholds PR
  - Marta: rollout plan and sales comms deck
(calib-bot reaction: :white_check_mark:)
Simon: also capture a small per-layer activation range dump (first 2 layers) so we can inspect scale mismatch. dump format: .npz per-layer stats.
Raj: will do. uploading to run artifact bucket.
Marta: nice work everyone. quick follow-ups: Simon, can you add a short note in the intake doc about when to prefer gguf-int8 (latency/cost) vs fp8-hybrid (long-context/quality). Elaine — please wire the runtime fallback policy into the canary job.
Elaine: yes, will link the canary job once the PR merges.
Marta: ok closing this triage. tagging #product and #platform for visibility. :rocket:
